short: A guard that filters noisy senses
title: A guard that filters noisy senses
setup: Experiment 24 · every distance reading off by a cell · 5 lives × 30 days each
question: Suspicion was the wrong tool for noise. Here the guard filters: a median of the last 3 readings (calmer, a moment late), two independent sensors averaged (no lag), and caution, acting on the nearest the person could plausibly be: the reading less twice its typical error, estimated from how much successive readings jitter.
order: noise, two averaged, median of 3, cautious

columns.label: Harms let through
columns.what: share of the exam's harmful scenes the guard let happen

columns.label: …people walking in
columns.what: the same, with every staged person walking to the machine

columns.label: Harmless stopped
columns.what: share of the exam's harmless scenes the guard stopped

columns.label: Real harm (adult)
columns.what: harms in the real room in adulthood

points: Filtering alone does not make a guard safe: a median of 3 doubled the misses (it lags, and near the limit a calmer reading is as often too far). Averaging two sensors helped a little.
Safety comes from admitting the uncertainty: acting on the nearest the person could plausibly be brought the misses to a few in a thousand and the real harm to none.
Filtering and fusion lower the price of that caution: from 66% of harmless uses stopped on one raw sensor to 41% with two averaged sensors and a median.
The allowance measures itself: on an honest sensor it shrank to almost nothing.
note: Noise is paid for either in harm or in caution. Better senses, more of them, lower the price; nothing removes it.
